scopeReview: IMP-2.B.1–2: demographic transition and epidemiological transition. Uses a four-stage classical schematic, not a universal timeline or exact country classification. Synthetic numbers and original questions; no external lesson/question text or figures copied.
varietyReview: Line-model interpretation, high/low-rate contrast, within-country fertility map and cause-of-death table; other tasks cover mechanisms, growth versus level, turnover, history, model complementarity, shocks and omitted migration. Varied keys/difficulty and all five skills.
repetitionReview: Not a numeric-only reprise of2.4: relates rate gaps to model stages and challenges model assumptions. Stage3 slower-positive growth, Stage4 turnover and Stage1/4 equal-gap comparison assess different misinterpretations. Mortality-cause counts are new.
referenceNote: Development verification only: classical framework/limits and original epidemiological theory. No third-party resource is added to the student catalog. Original synthetic examples and reasoning, no copied data/figures/questions.

questions.independentReview: Independently subtracted death from birth at each marker:42−40=2,40−15=25,25−9=16,10−10=0. Stage2 is the unique maximum. The connected markers are conceptual stages, not equal-duration historical observations.

questions.correctOption: A and D can have similarly slow natural increase while representing high-rate and low-rate conditions.
questions.independentReview: Recomputed gapsA1,B26,C14,D1 and compared component levelsA40/39 versusD10/9. Identical slow natural increase does not imply identical birth/mortality regimes.

questions.correctOption: A national label can conceal important subnational variation in fertility.
questions.independentReview: Compared four different district TFR values4.2,1.6,3.8,1.4. No mortality/time series is supplied, preventing exact district-stage assignment or a universal downward trend inference.

questions.correctOption: All deaths fell while chronic conditions became a larger share; infectious deaths still occurred.
questions.independentReview: Independently summed800+200=1000 and100+300=400, computed chronic shares.2/.75 and component changes−700/+100. The interpretation concerns aggregate composition, not complete elimination or individual outcomes.

questions.correctOption: Death rates may fall before birth rates fall substantially, widening the birth–death gap.
questions.independentReview: Held a relatively high birth rate and reduced death rate, yielding a larger positive difference. The mechanism is a lag between two natural-change components, not migration or instantaneous elimination of births.

questions.correctOption: Population continues to grow, but its rate of natural increase becomes smaller.
questions.independentReview: Used the inequalitiesbirth>death and decliningbirth with stabledeath: gap stayspositive but decreases. This verifies the direction of both level and rate without inventing an exact trajectory.

questions.correctOption: There are 500 births and 500 deaths, producing zero natural increase despite continuing demographic events.
questions.independentReview: Independently computed50000*10/1000=500 for each component and difference0. This verifies turnover under balance, distinct from assuming an empty or event-free population.

questions.correctOption: It is a simplified framework whose timing and pathways must be evaluated against local evidence.
questions.independentReview: Checked the difference between a conceptual sequence and an invariant historical timetable. The observed different pathways are compatible with a useful generalized framework but reject an exact universal schedule.

questions.correctOption: It examines changing mortality causes and disease patterns, helping explain changes in death rates.
questions.independentReview: Verified distinct explanatory targets: fertility/mortality levels versus mortality causes/patterns. Preserved complementarity without claiming a one-to-one universal stage correspondence or complete elimination of disease.

questions.correctOption: The disruption should be investigated with actual evidence rather than treated as an automatic permanent reset of the whole transition.
questions.independentReview: Held fertility low and varied mortality temporarily; there is no logical basis for inferring high births or permanent reversal. This is a model-limit question, not a real outbreak forecast or medical recommendation.

questions.correctOption: Net migration, because it can add to or offset the natural-change balance.
questions.independentReview: Checked the accounting identitytotalchange=births−deaths+immigrants−emigrants. The displayed two curves omit the last two terms; a stage label cannot recover their values.
